**Resubmitted: deviation at the fallback level, confidence 0.80 (propose_redline ok:true, minimality passed).** This is my single final submission.

Repair to the recurring deterministic failure:

- The check had no explicit notice figure to read — the prior grant said only "upon written notice". Operation 1 now states the fallback's own number in operative language: *"Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to TrueLink, and, subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the effective date of such termination."* I used sixty (60) days rather than thirty because sixty is the fallback element's own figure and I am not claiming preferred; it also caps the old month-end-following mechanic, which could run to sixty-one days (notice on 1 December ran to 31 January). TrueLink's duty to keep serving through the notice period and the Section 4 qualifier are retained.

Unchanged:

- Operation 2 cures the material breach — TrueLink's non-renewal notice rises from thirty (30) to **ninety (90)** days, so its only no-cause exit remains the end of a term, with our own 30-day notice preserved (fallback elements 3 and 4).
- Fallback element 2 stays **already_met**: no early-termination fee, penalty or unamortised charge exists anywhere; fees are charged per monthly invoice under Section 5(a).
- Preferred is not claimed (no flat 30-day notice, no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees).

Clean-up items for the next pass, outside this checklist: retarget Section 13's stale "Section 12 herein" cross-reference to Section 14, and fill the blank minimum support period in Section 4 so it cannot be argued to fetter the new convenience right.
